title: Supreme Court: Muldrow v. City of St. Louis
summary: An employee challenging a job transfer under Title VII must show that the transfer brought about some harm with respect to an identifiable term or condition of employment, but that harm need not be significant. (No. 22-193, opinion by Justice Kagan; 601 U.S. 346).

title: Supreme Court: McIntosh v. United States
summary: A district court’s failure to comply with Federal Rule of Criminal Procedure 32.2(b)(2)(B)’s requirement to enter a preliminary order imposing criminal forfeiture before sentencing does not bar a judge from ordering forfeiture at sentencing subject to harmless-error principles on appellate review. (No. 22-7386, opinion by Justice Sotomayor; 601 U.S. 330).

title: Supreme Court: Rudisill v. McDonough
summary: Servicemembers who, through separate periods of service, accrue educational benefits under both the Montgomery and Post-9/11 GI Bills may use either one, in any order, up to 38 U. S. C. §3695(a)’s 48-month aggregate-benefits cap. (No. 22-888, opinion by Justice Jackson; 601 U.S. 294).

title: Supreme Court: DeVillier v. Texas
summary: Owners of property north of U. S. Interstate Highway 10 adversely affected by the flood evacuation barrier constructed by Texas should be permitted on remand to pursue their Takings Clause claims through the cause of action available under Texas law. (No. 22-913, opinion by Justice Thomas; 601 U.S. 285).

title: Supreme Court: Sheetz v. El Dorado County
summary: The Fifth Amendment’s Takings Clause does not distinguish between legislative and administrative land-use permit conditions. (No. 22-1074, opinion by Justice Barrett; 601 U.S. 267).

title: Supreme Court: Macquarie Infrastructure Corp. v. Moab Partners, L. P.
summary: Pure omissions are not actionable under SEC Rule 10b–5(b), which makes it unlawful to omit material facts in connection with buying or selling securities when that omission renders “statements made” misleading. (No. 22-1165, opinion by Justice Sotomayor; 601 U.S. 257).

title: Supreme Court: Bissonnette v. LePage Bakeries Park St., LLC
summary: A transportation worker need not work in the transportation industry to be exempt from coverage under §1 of the Federal Arbitration Act, 9 U. S. C. §1 et seq. (No. 23-51, opinion by Chief Justice Roberts; 601 U.S. 246).
